summary: Config review request: multi-region ingesters causing staggered 429s during bulk ingest
description:
Issue summary:
StreamDocs is seeing periodic 429s during a daily bulk ingest that fans out across workers in two regions. The pattern is staggered: us-east workers begin getting 429 responses ~09:02 UTC and eu-west workers ~09:08 UTC, coinciding with their local warmup requests.

Impact:
- Intermittent failed uploads for their ingestion pipeline (10–25% of batches).
- Increased retry traffic and higher than expected token/billing counts for the customer.
- Customer requesting configuration guidance and short-term mitigation while we investigate root cause.

Environment:
- Customer tier: enterprise (StreamDocs Inc.) with reserved Dedicated capacity in both us-east-1 and eu-west-1.
- Ingest topology: 24 workers in each region, each worker creates ephemeral API keys on startup and multiplexes HTTP/2 connections through a shared NAT gateway IP pool.
- Warmup behaviour: customers run scheduled model warmups and a bursty prefix cache priming before main ingest.

Steps to reproduce (as reported):
1) At ~09:00 UTC the customer performs scheduled warmup (parallel small requests to priming API).
2) At 09:01–09:10 they start concurrent workers for bulk ingest (each opens short-lived ephemeral keys and streams file chunks).
3) Observed: 5xxs are rare, but 429s spike in windows that align with worker startup; console shows per-route token quota near exhaustion even though per-tenant dashboard shows available credits.

Observed behavior:
- 429s returned with X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 and X-RateLimit-Reset: small number of seconds.
- Throttling appears to be applied unevenly across regions and across connections behind the same NAT IPs.
- Customer reports that rotating ephemeral keys while multiple workers start amplifies occurrence.

Expected behavior:
- Bulk ingest should not encounter tenant-level throttles given their reserved capacity and purchased burst allowances.
- Warmups and short-lived keys should not lead to large, synchronized token accounting that blocks streaming sessions.

Logs / headers attached by customer (excerpt):
- curl response headers: X-RateLimit-Limit: 600000, X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, X-RateLimit-Reset: 18
- Example request ids: rq_12a3, rq_12a4 (us-east), rq_9b7c (eu-west)

Temporary mitigations customer tried:
- Staggering worker start by 30s reduced the amplitude but did not eliminate 429s.
- Switching to one long-lived key (instead of per-worker ephemeral keys) during ingest eliminated 429s for a test window.

Request from customer:
- Configuration review: recommended guardrails for combining ephemeral keys + multi-region warmups + reserved capacity.
- Short-term workaround to avoid further ingestion failures and billing surprises.
comments: 2026-03-12 10:15 - Ayesha Patel: Created ticket after initial Slack thread with customer (#support-streamdocs). Customer provided aggregated logs and Grafana links.

2026-03-12 12:03 - Support (Liam Chen): Acknowledged receipt; asked for exact worker start timestamps, ephemeral key TTLs, and NAT gateway public IP list for correlation. Set priority P1 due to ingestion failures.

2026-03-12 14:22 - Customer (StreamDocs SRE - Maria Gonzales): Provided timestamps and confirmed ephemeral key TTL=300s, worker fanout=24, NAT uses 3 public IPs per region. Attached sample request IDs.

2026-03-13 09:40 - Support (Liam Chen): Correlated request IDs with rate-limiter logs; initial hypothesis posted to ticket. Requested permission to run a short test that disables ephemeral key rotation for 15 minutes.
2026-03-13 11:05 - Customer: Approved test. Reported elimination of 429s during the test window when using a single long-lived key.

2026-03-14 08:55 - Infra (SRE - Priya Rao): Noted NAT pool reuse and healthcheck probe patterns that may increment token accounting. Proposed changes to token attribution logic for short-lived keys (engineering follow-up).
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12: Pull logs from rate-limiter cluster (rl-01..03) for the provided request IDs. Observed that counts are attributed both to api-key and to source_ip in different internal stages, leading to temporary double-counting in the enforcement window.

2026-03-12: Grafana (rate-limiter/tenant/StreamDocs): Tenant-level tokens drop briefly but still within purchased quota; however per-route buckets (short-window) show exhaustion consistent with staggered fanout spikes.

2026-03-13: Replayed a controlled startup (customer-provided script) in staging. Reproduced 429s when ephemeral key rotation coincided with healthcheck probes; switching to single key removed the error.

2026-03-13: Observed NAT IP pooling pattern: multiple workers behind same IP cause per-connection accounting to aggregate at proxy layer; with ephemeral keys this leads to many unique key+ip pairs within the same enforcement window increasing bookkeeping overhead and triggering short-window per-route limits.

2026-03-14: Noted related known behaviors: short refill windows for per-route throttle and high-cardinality key churn can drive apparent throttles even when tenant quotas exist (see runbook link). Opened a ticket with rate-limiter team to evaluate attribution logic and whether to prioritize tenant-level allowances over per-route short-window enforcement for dedicated customers.
References: Grafana panel https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rl/tenant-overview?orgId=1&var-tenant=streamdocs, kube logs https://logs.redwood.ai/streamdocs/rl-01 (internal access).
resolution_notes: Short-term recommended mitigations provided to customer (applied on 2026-03-13):
- Use a single long-lived API key for the bulk ingest window instead of creating per-worker ephemeral keys. This removed 429s in customer's test and is the fastest mitigation.
- Stagger worker starts by >=60s and avoid running warmups that generate concurrent priming traffic from all workers. This reduces synchronized spikes on per-route windows.
- Disable or reduce outbound healthcheck frequency during the ingest window to avoid hidden token drains from probes.
- Rate-limiter team will evaluate attribution logic: ensure tenant/reserved capacity overrides short-window per-route enforcement for enterprise/dedicated customers. (Engineering ticket created).
- Consider increasing per-route short refill window and allowing burst buffer for requests originating from same tenant but different ephemeral keys behind shared NAT IPs.

- Add a console warning and prescriptive template for customers using ephemeral keys in high-fanout ingestion topologies that outlines best practices (long-lived key option, staging warmups, staggered start).
Owner: Support (Liam Chen) for customer guidance; Rate-limiter eng (Priya Rao) for infra change. Target ETA for infra evaluation: 2 weeks.
Status: Customer applied short-term mitigations and ingestion stability improved. Engineering follow-up pending; keep ticket open until infra changes are evaluated.
